scenes.title: Backoff is calling a busy friend
scenes.body: Their line is busy. You don't redial every second; you wait a little, then **a bit longer each time**. If a thousand people do the same, a little **randomness** stops them all calling back at the same moment.

items.q: Which API errors should you retry, and how?
items.a: Retry **429, 5xx and network errors** with exponential backoff plus jitter, and a cap on attempts. Don't retry other 4xx errors: they fail the same way until you fix the request or the key.
items.trap: Retrying every error in a tight loop. That hammers the server and burns rate limit.

items.q: Why catch specific exceptions before general ones?
items.a: Python runs the **first matching `except`**. A parent class like `APIStatusError` matches every HTTP error, so if it comes first, the specific handlers never run.
items.trap: A bare `except Exception:` that hides bugs and swallows the error details.

scenes.question: Which error should your code retry?
scenes.explain: A 429 recovers after waiting. 400, 401 and 404 fail the same way every time until you fix the request or the key.

items.text: 4xx (except 429): fix the request or the key; don't retry
429, 5xx, network: retry with backoff; the SDK does it for you
Catch specific exception classes before `APIStatusError`
Cost = tokens × price; count, track and budget
